We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (i.e., one disconnection) for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's a bicyclic? There's a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene? The SMILES: CH2=C( aromatic ring )C@@H1CH2CH2CH2C@@1(OH)C(F)(F)F. So a cyclopentanol fused? Actually C@@H1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@1(OH)] is a cyclopentanol (five-membered ring) with OH at carbon 13 (bridge). That carbon also attached to C(F)(F)F (CF3). So the target is a cyclopentanol with CF3 substituent and attached to an exocyclic alkene bearing phenyl.

The guidance mentions carbonyl-ene reaction forward: carbonyl + alkene -> new C-C bond, forming hydroxyl and five-membered ring. So retrosynthetically, we can break the C-O bond (hydroxyl) to a carbonyl (ketone) and break the C-C bond formed to a C=C double bond (alkene). So the precursor would be a ketone (maybe cyclopentanone) with an alkene (phenyl-substituted) that undergoes carbonyl-ene to give the product.

Thus we need a template that corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (retro: break C-O to C=O, break C-C to C=C). We need to find a template ID that matches. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken: "aliphatic hydroxyls"? Actually forward reaction forms aliphatic hydroxyl, so broken functional group is "ketones". Also C-C double bonds are broken (the alkene becomes C-C). So functional_groups_broken: ["ketones", "C-C double bonds"]; functional_groups_formed: ["aliphatic hydroxyls", "five-membered rings"] maybe. Also bonds formed: maybe C-C bond formed? In forward, C-C bond formed, C-O bond formed, C=C bond broken, C=O broken. So for retrosynthesis, we need template that breaks C-O and forms C=O? Actually we just need a template that matches forward carbonyl-ene. Let's search.
